ai_show_review.summary: Jazzy Clementine suite with tight New Potato and swing Spanish Jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The set rolls out a seamless jazzy suite beginning with the first performance of “Clementine” and moving through “New Potato Caboose,” “Born Cross‑Eyed,” and an expansive “Spanish Jam.” Jerry’s spacious guitar tone and Pigpen’s organ drive a swinging groove, while the band delivers one of its strongest pre‑1970 performances.
ai_show_review.review: Eureka Municipal Auditorium, January 20 1968 captured a rare early‑Dead moment: the first ever rendition of Phil Lesh’s “Clementine” opening a fluid, jazz‑inflected suite. From the opening jam into “Clementine,” the band glides through “New Potato Caboose” and “Born Cross‑Eyed” with effortless transitions, then launches into a soaring “Spanish Jam” that showcases Jerry Garcia’s lyrical lead guitar and Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s organ in top form. The set closes with a brief but intense fragment of “Dark Star” after a tight “Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks),” leaving the audience with a swinging, almost suite‑like feel that many reviewers call one of the best pre‑1970 shows. All five soundboard sources are crystal‑clear; the Clugston recording in particular preserves every instrument without dropouts, making it the definitive listen for anyone wanting to experience this historic, jazzy chapter of the Dead’s evolution.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture with full set, no dropouts, and exceptional instrument separation.

key_highlights: First performance of “Clementine” – a jazzy, Coltrane‑inflected suite opener.
"New Potato Caboose" > "Born Cross‑Eyed" sequence delivers spacious guitar and tight rhythm.
"Spanish Jam" showcases soaring lead guitar and Pigpen’s organ in top form.
Swinging drumming from Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann drives the jazz feel throughout.

band_performance.Jerry: Spacious, deliberate guitar tone on “New Potato Caboose,” jazzy lead on “Clementine,” and soaring solo in the “Spanish Jam"; vocals on “Clementine" praised.
band_performance.Phil: Co‑writer of “Clementine," bass work infused with Coltrane influence; strong fire playing throughout, especially leading the “Caution" jam.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ at his best – deep, jazzy texture that drives the suite, with a "My Favorite Things" vibe on “Clementine" and essential depth in all jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Swinging cymbal work and emphatic drumming propel the jazz‑inflected feel of the set.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers tight, high‑energy early‑68 drumming alongside Mickey, reinforcing the groove throughout.
